newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany to permit bond stripping from middle 1997.
newsitem.headline: Germany to permit bond stripping from middle 1997.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Friday said that the German government would permit the stripping of its 10 and 30-year bonds from July 1997.
At the same time the Bundesbank said Bonn would issue a strippable 30-year bond in the middle of the year which it plans to top up at a later date.

Both the government's already issued 6.25 percent bond maturing in 2024 and the new bond of 1997 would also be strippable, the Bundesbank said. It has set January 4 and July 4 as dates when issues can be stripped.
Germany to permit bond stripping from middle 1997
Stripping a bond means that it is separated into the principal and coupons, which are then sold separately with the principal becoming a zero-coupon security.

Until now bond stripping was not permitted in Germany, and analysts say the move, which has been debated for some time, marks another step forward in Germany's efforts to improve its position as a leading financial market.

The Bundesbank also said the government plans to issue one 10-year bond with a volume of up to 15 billion marks in the first ten days of January and top up the issue, with a volume of up to 10 billion marks in the third ten days of January.
In the first quarter the government plans to issue a total of up to 54 billion marks in new debt, the Bundesbank said.
